body:
Author-side corollaries of the unchanged PR #176 expansion; offered for the analytic reviewers, NOT a new independent verdict and no file bytes changed.

Write c=C2/C0. From §4 equation (15), the normalized radial density is
p_t(q)=11 q^-12 [1+c t^-2((13/11)q^-2-1)] + O(t^-4 q^-12)
in the weighted sense used there. Therefore for every fixed real p<11,

E[(R/t)^p | R>t]
 = 11/(11-p)
   - [2p c / ((13-p)(11-p))] t^-2
   + O_p(t^-4).

The coefficient follows exactly from
13/(13-p)-11/(11-p) = -2p/[(13-p)(11-p)].
The restriction p<11 is sharp for the Pareto limiting moment. This is AFTER the original r->0 limit and does not imply finite-r moment convergence.

Differentiating the moment identity at p=0 (justified by the same q^-12 envelope on a fixed neighborhood of p=0) gives the log-radius correction

E[log(R/t) | R>t]
 = 1/11 - (2c/143) t^-2 + O(t^-4).

There is also an explicit fixed-upper-tail quantile correction. If Q_alpha(t) is defined by
P(R/t > Q_alpha(t) | R>t)=alpha, 0<alpha<1 fixed,
then equation (17) and a one-variable implicit expansion give

Q_alpha(t)
 = alpha^(-1/11) [
     1 + (c/11)(alpha^(2/11)-1)t^-2 + O_alpha(t^-4)
   ].

At the exact aligned-planar scope of §7, c>4587/856>0, so every fixed upper-tail quantile approaches its Pareto limit from below at second order, and E log(R/t) approaches 1/11 from below. This is an asymptotic coefficient/sign statement for each fixed model; it is NOT a model-uniform finite-threshold inequality because the O(t^-4) remainder is not uniform in L,k,b.

These are direct consequences of the frozen proof65f24b1f and can be checked inside Slice B without enlarging the source interface.
